inputs.base_revenue_note: FY26 continuing-operations operating revenue on the OFR basis (Asset Management 880.5 + Corporate Trust 220.8 + Group & Support 39.4; FY2026 AR line 6787). Wealth Management (233.7, discontinued) is excluded because it is sold to Bain Capital inside year 1 of the horizon and sits in the equity bridge as sale proceeds instead. The Metrics.csv RevenueContinuing of 1,156.3 is the statutory figure, which grosses up 15.6 of structured-product income matched by a 9.7 distributions expense.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 115.7m ordinary shares on issue (FY2026 AR line 297) plus 3.37m dilutive potential ordinary shares (diluted weighted average 116,674,625 less basic 113,303,375, AR line 8515-8517). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. No buyback in FY26 and none announced; DRP is not operating.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings 627.5 carrying (629.3 face, syndicated facility refinanced May 2025) less cash held by continuing operations 330.2 at 30 June 2026 (AR lines 5469, 7654). Lease liabilities of 113.1 are EXCLUDED under lease treatment B. WM's 1.6 cash and 41.7 lease liabilities sit in the held-for-sale disposal group and leave with the sale. Part of the 330.2 is regulatory capital for AFSL/trustee licences and is not freely distributable; not haircut here, disclosed as a risk.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR cash-flow reconciliation share-based payment add-back 20.4 (group incl. WM; CSV StockBasedComp). Australian filer; no net-share-settlement withholding line, so no equity-award tax to add. Statutory continuing equity remuneration expense was 17.2 (11.7 underlying + 4.2 Pendal retention + 1.2 Simplification), AR line 6963.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported_fcf 256.5 (OCF 272.3 - capex 15.8, group incl. WM) - SBC 20.4 - interest received 13.2 = 222.9. This is a levered, whole-group figure after 43.0 of interest paid and 42.0 of pre-tax one-off simplification/transaction cash costs, and before the 25.1 of lease payments charged under treatment B; it is retained for auditability only. The forward build starts from continuing-operations components, not from this number.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:15:22Z (intraday ASX session; 52-week range 15.10-21.41; price is four days after the 21-Sep-2026 EQT engagement conclusion that took the stock down ~14%)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, single rate across scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows). Risk-free AUD 10-year ~4.3% (Sep 2026), ERP 5.5%, equity beta 1.15 for a listed active manager with market-linked fee revenue -> cost of equity ~10.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.3% (BBSY plus margin on the syndicated facility), ~4.4% after 30% tax. Market weights at 30 June: equity ~2.0bn / debt 0.63bn = 76/24 -> ~9.1%; the WM sale proceeds retire most of the debt, moving the mix toward equity, so 9.5% is used as the through-horizon rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The full lease payment (principal + interest, 25.1 in FY26 financing 'Lease payments', AR line 7644) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.7% of continuing revenue (~19.4m, the continuing share after WM's 41.7 of lease liabilities leave with the disposal group). Lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (continuing underlying D&A 33.8 less ~15 ROU depreciation implied by the lease cash split) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; the 30% minority in Interfi Systems (NCI 14.2 at 30 June 2026, AR line 7511, acquired 19 June 2026) is deducted once in the equity bridge. Barrow Hanley employee-owned units are a compensation instrument and are inside the underlying expense base, not a separate NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2, operating company non-US, with owner-fcf-adaptations for leases, NCI and an excluded income stream). Perpetual is a fee-based operating company (active asset management + corporate trustee/custody), not a bank, REIT or LIC: it has real capex, real working capital, a conventional debt facility and unlevered operating cash flow, so the owner-FCF engine applies. The 'live takeover' row does not apply: EQT's four proposals (A$21.64 to A$22.50, Jul-Sep 2026) were all rejected and the board said engagement concluded on 21-Sep-2026; there is no scheme to weight. The Bain Capital WM sale IS a live transaction but it is a divestment of a segment, handled by valuing continuing operations only and adding net sale proceeds in the equity bridge. INTEREST INCOME STRIPPED: continuing interest income 10.5 (AR line 6742) is inside UPBT and is removed from the EBITDA anchor because the cash that earns it is credited in the bridge (matching-asset rule). SBC-ZERO does not apply (equity remuneration ~1.5% of revenue), so house and street bases differ and band_position is meaningful. ONE-OFFS EXCLUDED FROM THE BASE: FY24 goodwill impairment (547m J O Hambro/TSW), FY25 and FY26 TSW impairments (63.5 in FY26), 80.6 of acquired-intangible amortisation, 29.2 of WM-sale costs and 12.8 of Simplification costs are all outside the continuing underlying anchor. FY0 anchor: continuing UPBT 251.7 + D&A 33.8 + financing costs 47.8 = underlying EBITDA 333.3; + equity remuneration 11.7 - interest income 10.5 = 334.5 pre-SBC, ex-interest, post-nothing-for-leases = 29.3% of 1,140.7. Cash tax: FY26 income taxes paid were 8.6 (FY25 30.9) against a 26% underlying continuing tax charge, sheltered by capital losses, prior-year adjustments and US tax amortisation of acquired intangibles; the cash rate ramps 15% -> 28% over five years rather than perpetuating the shelter. Working capital capture 0%: fee businesses have no deferred-revenue tailwind. The 30-Jun-2026 cash still contains the 63cps FY26 final dividend (72.9m) that the current ex-dividend price no longer carries, so it is deducted in the bridge.

equity_bridge.item: Wealth Management sale to Bain Capital: 500.0 upfront consideration less ~27 cash tax on the gain (68.6 accounting tax recognised less the 41.4 net benefit from capital losses and the higher tax cost base, AR lines 8218, 8261) less ~18 of residual completion/separation costs
equity_bridge.note: Completion targeted Q4 CY2026 subject to ACCC, FIRB, ASIC AFSL variations and court schemes. The up-to-50 incremental upfront (advice-business performance, unlikely with WM UPBT down 15% in FY26) and the up-to-50 two-year earn-out are EXCLUDED and belong to the bull narrative. If the deal breaks (the 2024 KKR precedent), WM retained is worth roughly 300 (UPBT 44.0 -> ~31 NPAT at ~10x), i.e. ~A$1.30/share less than this bridge item; that risk is carried in the 30% bear weight, not in a fourth scenario.
AR line 7511; flows are consolidated, NCI deducted once here.

equity_bridge.item: FY26 final dividend 63cps declared, unfranked, in 30-Jun cash but not in the ex-dividend price
equity_bridge.note: 63c x 115.7m shares. Paid in the September quarter per Perpetual's usual timetable; the 25-Sep-2026 price is ex-entitlement.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward judgment (average of the base-case continuing-revenue path); every historical CAGR is acquisition-distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+11.1%) diverges from EPS 5yr (-10.6%) by far more than 30%, and equity 3yr (-13.4%) diverges from revenue 3yr (+10.4%). Both are artefacts: Barrow Hanley (FY21) and the Pendal scrip merger (Jan 2023) roughly doubled revenue, equity and the share count (56.2m -> 116.7m), and the FY24 impairment (-472 NPAT) then wrote 630m of that equity back off. Revenue per share went 11.6 (FY21) -> 11.9 (FY26), ~0.5%/yr, which is the honest organic number.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs use total group revenue (FY26 1,390.0 incl. WM; FY23 1,034.1; FY21 652.1) so the series is like-for-like; the CSV's FY2026 Revenue cell is continuing-only. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY21 93.8, FY23 63.5, FY26 222.9. The owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (18.9%) is above the reported-FCF 5yr CAGR (19.2%) only because FY21 SBC was proportionally larger; SBC has not outgrown cash flow (SBC 12.3 -> 20.4 on a ~2.1x larger revenue base). None of these CAGRs are used to set forward growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 -2%: AM enters the year with a -84.2m annualised net revenue outcome from -25.1bn of FY26 outflows (~-9% of AM revenue) only partly offset by market appreciation and Active ETF inflows, against Corporate Trust +7-8%. FY28 flat as outflows moderate under the new J O Hambro CEO; from FY29 growth settles at 2-2.5%, i.e. CT growth plus market beta minus continued net outflows.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 anchor 29.3%. FY27 dips to 28.8% because revenue falls faster than the remaining ~5-10m of Simplification savings (72.6m of the 70-80m target already delivered) can offset, and WM separation leaves some stranded cost; recovers to 29.5% by FY30 and holds. No structural margin expansion is assumed for a business losing scale in AM.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax paid 8.6 in FY26 (30.9 in FY25) vs a 26% underlying charge; ramps to 28% (just under the 30% statutory, allowing for the long-lived US tax amortisation of acquired intangibles) over five years.
base.terminal_rationale: 12x owner FCF cap (below the 20x default): an active manager with structural outflows should not be capitalised as a compounder; ASX peers Platinum and Magellan have traded 6-12x, Pinnacle far higher but it is a different model. Terminal growth 2.0%.

bull.rationale: AM outflows stabilise in FY27 (JOH turnaround, Barrow Hanley value cycle, Active ETF and fixed income wins) and markets stay supportive; Corporate Trust compounds at high single digits with Interfi and the IAM term-deposit business adding to Digital and Markets. Simplification reaches the top of the 70-80m range and the WM separation strands little cost, taking the margin to 32.5% by FY31. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap held at 12x.

bear.rationale: The passive shift keeps AM net outflows at FY26's pace (-10%/yr of AUM) for two more years and a market drawdown compounds it; only 51% of funds meet 3-year objectives so redemptions persist at JOH, TSW and Trillium. Operating deleverage takes the margin to 25% despite the cost-out. Corporate Trust still grows but cannot offset. Terminal growth 1%, cap 10x. The WM deal-break case (~A$1.30/share) is additional to these flows and is why bear carries 30%.

scenario_narratives.base: Perpetual after the Bain sale is an Asset Management franchise in managed decline (net outflows of -25.1bn in FY26 on 224bn AUM, an annualised net revenue outcome of -84.2m against a -23.9m target) bolted to a genuinely good Corporate Trust business (revenue +8%, UPBT +9%, FUA 1.35tn, 10-year Trustee of the Year). The base case has continuing revenue falling 2% in FY27 as the outflow run-rate lands, flat in FY28, then 2-2.5%/yr as market beta and Corporate Trust outgrow a slower AM bleed. Margins hold near 29-29.5% (the 72.6m of Simplification savings is largely in the FY26 base already), cash tax normalises to 28%, and net proceeds of ~455m from WM retire most of the 627.5m facility. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF, which is what the market has paid for mid-tier active managers with flat-to-declining AUM.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are (1) AM flows: the new J O Hambro CEO's simplification restores performance, Barrow Hanley benefits from a value cycle, and Active ETFs (DIFF raised 295m in its first year) and fixed income diversify distribution so net flows turn neutral by FY28; (2) Corporate Trust keeps compounding at high single digits with Interfi and the IAM term-deposit business expanding Digital and Markets AUA (+14% in FY26); (3) the WM separation strands little cost and Simplification lands at the top of the 70-80m range, lifting the group margin to 32.5%. The 50m incremental upfront and 50m earn-out from Bain (excluded from the bridge) and renewed M&A interest, with EQT having shown A$22.50 of willingness, are upside on top of the modelled flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are (1) the structural active-to-passive shift: outflows continue at FY26's pace for two more years, and a market drawdown hits ad valorem fees and flows at once, so AM revenue falls 15-20% cumulatively; (2) further impairments and a fourth consecutive year of statutory losses undermine dividend capacity; (3) the Bain transaction fails or slips, as the KKR deal did in 2024 when an adverse ATO ruling roughly tripled the expected tax cost, leaving Perpetual with 627.5m of gross debt against ~330m of continuing EBITDA and no franking recovery. With EQT gone and a persistent 'Hold' consensus, there is no bid support for the price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because two independent adverse paths are live: AM outflows are structural and accelerating (net revenue outcome missed target by 60m in FY26) and the WM sale still needs ACCC, FIRB, ASIC and court approvals with the KKR collapse as a precedent, and the bridge assumes it closes. Bull cut to 20% because it needs a JOH turnaround, benign markets and a clean separation to all land together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the continuing Asset Management + Corporate Trust business on unlevered owner FCF (SBC and lease cash expensed, interest income stripped, cash tax normalised), add the net cash from selling Wealth Management, deduct net debt, the Interfi minority and the dividend already paid out of 30 June cash, and cap the terminal at 12x because a manager with structural outflows should not be valued as a compounder. EQT's rejected A$22.50 is treated as evidence of what a financial buyer would pay, not as a floor: the engagement is over.
key_risks_to_valuation: AM net outflows: every -10bn of AUM is roughly -40m of revenue at the 44bps margin; the base assumes the bleed slows from FY28, which is a judgment not yet evidenced by flows
WM sale completion: the bridge carries ~455m of net proceeds; a deal break removes ~A$1.30/share and leaves gross debt at 627.5m
Cash tax: the 15% -> 28% ramp is a judgment on how long US intangible amortisation and capital losses shelter cash tax; a slower ramp adds value, faster removes it
Regulatory capital inside the 330.2 of cash is not freely distributable; no haircut applied
Market beta: ad valorem fees on ~224bn AUM make every scenario a function of equity markets management does not control
Terminal multiple: 12x owner FCF binds in base and bull; Gordon at 9.5%/2% would be ~13.6x
